solves.reasoning: (A) perceptual (지각의) is correct — the brain recognizes objects via perception, not conceptual (개념적). (B) flexibility (유연성) — the brain's immense flexibility allows route-switching; rigidity contradicts this. (C) navigate (항법) — migrating birds use stars to navigate; stagnate (정체) makes no sense.

(A) illuminations — objects recognized under changing illuminations (lighting); eliminations makes no sense. (B) vicarious — the brain's route-switching is 'vicarious functioning'; victorious is wrong. (C) sufficient — 'only a few lines are sufficient' to recognize caricatures; insufficient contradicts the passage.

(A) extraordinarily — 'It is extraordinarily adapted'; ordinarily would mean weakly adapted, contradicting the passage. (B) biological — vicarious functioning is in most biological systems; biographical is about life stories, unrelated. (C) external — 'the brain relies on external features such as hair'; internal was already mentioned as 'hardly visible', so external is used as backup.

① 'conceptual' is wrong: the passage refers to the human 'perceptual' (지각적) system designed to recognize objects. A conceptual (개념적) system deals with abstract ideas, not object recognition under changing lighting.
③ 'insufficient' is wrong: passage says 'only a few lines are sufficient' — even in extreme cases a few lines suffice for face recognition. Insufficient (불충분한) directly contradicts the original.
② 'exposed' is wrong: passage says 'parts of a face are covered' (가려진) — exposed (드러난) is the opposite. When parts are covered, recognition still works via external features.
Blank: 'This immense ___ of the brain to rely on changing cues'. The passage is about the brain's ability to switch routes = flexibility (유연성). Rigidity/complexity/sensitivity don't fit.

Blank: 'is known as ___ functioning'. The brain's ability to use alternative routes when one is blocked = vicarious functioning. This is the key term in the passage. Autonomous/simultaneous/deliberate don't match.

Blank: 'recognize the face of a celebrity in ___'. The passage describes recognizing faces in simplified drawings = caricatures (캐리커처). Portraits are realistic, sculptures are 3D, photographs are photos — caricatures made with 'just a few pencil strokes' is the original context.
immense = enormous (거대한). Moderate (중간), minimal (최소), gradual (점진적) are all wrong. Immense means extremely large/vast.
sufficient = adequate (충분한). Excessive (과도한) is too much, essential (필수적인) means necessary, abundant (풍부한) means plentiful. Adequate best matches 'sufficient' (충분한).
cues = signals (단서/신호). Obstacles (장애물), patterns (패턴), boundaries (경계) don't match. Cues are signals/hints the brain uses to recognize — signals is the closest synonym.
internal의 반의어 = external (외부의). The passage itself uses this pair: 'internal features' vs 'external features'. Hidden (숨겨진), central, primary are not antonyms.
recognize의 반의어 = overlook (간과하다). Examine/detect/observe are all synonyms of recognize. Overlook means to miss/fail to notice — the opposite of recognizing.

(A) 'If one is blocked, it takes another route' — route = 경로/방법 (the brain's processing pathway). (B) 'scenic route through the mountains' — route = 도로/길 (physical road). So (A)경로/방법 - (B)도로/길 = choice 3.
'Experienced or felt through the actions/experiences of another rather than directly' = vicarious (대리의). Simultaneous (동시의), spontaneous (자발적), autonomous (자율적) don't match this definition.
illuminate (동사) → illuminations (명사 복수형). 'Under changing illuminations' = 변화하는 조명 환경 아래서. Noun plural form of illuminate.
The stem says 'visible → 어법에 맞게' — the passage already uses 'are hardly visible'. The adjective 'visible' is correct as predicate adjective after 'hardly'. No change needed — answer is 'visible'.

Blank: 'migrating birds fly thousands of miles and may rely on the stars to ___'. The context is navigation over long distances using stars = navigate (항법하다). Communicate/hibernate/reproduce don't fit.

Blank: 'cloudy day, they may instead rely on ___ or their magnetic sense'. The birds switch from stars to alternative cues = landmarks (지형지물). Instincts/companions/predictions don't match the passage's specific example.
